1: In the name of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one God.
This is the Sinodos of the house of the church, which the apostles gave by the hand of Clement, which they sent forth of old.
1.1: [Topic:] Concerning the number of bishops that are necessary in the ordination of a bishop.
1.2: A bishop shall be ordained by two or by three bishops; but an elder and a deacon, and the rest of the ordained — let them be ordained by one bishop.

2.1: [Topic:] Concerning the things that it is fitting to bring upon the altar.
2.2: If a bishop or an elder brings anything upon the altar of the Lord, apart from what we have commanded — anything he brings and presents as an offering — or he brings honey, or milk, or of birds, or of any other beast, besides what our Lord commanded: let him be deposed.
2.3: And they shall not be allowed to bring anything upon the altar except ears of grain and grapes in their season, and pure oil of the lamps, and frankincense at the time of the holy eucharist.
2.4: But the other remaining fruits, let them be sent into the house, and let them be for the bishop and for the elders; but let them not bring them upon the altar.
2.5: And let the bishop and the elders and the rest of the ordained divide them among themselves.

3.1: [Topic:] A bishop, an elder, and a deacon shall not reject [his wife] under pretext for the sake of the service of the Lord.
3.2: And if they have rejected [her], let them be separated [from the church]; and if they do not restore her and bring her back, let them be deposed.

4.1: [Topic:] Concerning the day on which it is fitting to celebrate the Pascha.
4.2: And if a bishop, or an elder, or a deacon celebrates the holy Pascha with the Jews before the night and the day are made equal — let him be deposed.

5.1: [Topic:] A bishop, an elder, and a deacon shall not mix themselves in with the doings of this world.
5.2: And if they mix themselves in, let them be separated [from the church].

6.1: [Topic:] If a bishop, or one of the priests, who has not received the eucharist at the time of the solemnization, declares the reason for this — and if there is what made him unworthy — let him be forgiven.
6.2: But if he does not declare his reason, let him be expelled; for he became a leader, that sin should come upon the people, and he made them take offense at him who offered the eucharist, as though he had not offered it in purity.

7.1: Every believer who enters the church of the Christians, and hears the Scriptures, and does not stand while they make the prayers, and does not partake of our holy eucharist — over him let them not pray; and as is fitting, let him be expelled; for he has caused strife and disturbance to the Christian church.

8.1: And if anyone prays with him who does not partake of the mysteries — even though it be at home — let him be expelled.

9.1: [Topic:] And let them not pray with him who has been expelled.
9.2: And if one of the priests prays with one priest who has been expelled, let him also be expelled.

10.1: And if one of the priests or a layman who has been expelled goes into a city, as though he had not been expelled, and enters this city without permission, and is ordained — let him be expelled, he and the one who ordained him.
10.2: And if he was outside, let him be expelled; put him outside for a longer time; for he has lied to the church of God.

11.1: [Topic:] It is not allowed for a bishop to leave his diocese and be ordained in another.
11.2: And if the people urge him — except for the sake of benefit — and they urge him that he do this, for he is able: he will benefit them through these, by the word of righteousness.
11.3: And let him not do this by himself alone, but by the judgment of many bishops, and by a very strong urging.

12.1: If an elder or a deacon, or any of the grade of the priesthood, leaves his post and goes to another place and dwells in that place a long time, without permission — we, the bishops, command that he never again minister. And moreover, if the bishop sent to him to return to his place and he did not listen to him, let him be expelled from his office, and let him approach the place where he was as a layman.
12.2: And if the bishop with whom he was receives him as one of the priests, and regards this ordinance which we established as void, let this bishop also be expelled, as a teacher of the transgression of the law.

13.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who marries two [women], or a concubine.
13.2: He who marries two women, or a widow, after his baptism, cannot be ordained as a bishop or an elder or a deacon, nor shall he at all be numbered with the ordained priests.
13.3: He who marries a concubine, or a woman who has become suspected, or a woman who has been violated, or a harlot, or a maidservant, or a woman who appears in the theatre — he shall not be ordained as a bishop or an elder or a deacon, and he shall not at all be counted among the ordained priests. And he who dwells with two sisters, or with the daughter of his brother — he shall not be able to become a priest.

14.1: A priest who becomes security for a man shall be deposed.

15.2: If he has become a eunuch by men by force, or if they have cut off his organ in war, or if he was born thus — and they deem him worthy — let him be ordained as bishop.
15.3: But if he castrated himself of his own will, he cannot become one of the ordained; for he became a slayer of himself and an enemy of the creature of God.
15.4: And if one of the ordained cuts off his organ, let him be deposed; for he is a slayer of himself, he alone.
15.5: And a layman who castrates himself, let him be expelled three years; for he is an enemy of his own life.

16.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who commits sexual immorality, or swears falsely, or steals.
16.2: A bishop or an elder or a deacon who is found in sexual immorality, or in swearing falsely, or in theft — let him be deposed, but let him not be expelled; for God says: he shall not be punished twice for the crime.

17.1: [Topic:] And also with reference to the rest of the ordained.
17.2: Those who are readers and psalmsingers: if they enter into the priesthood and desire to marry, let them marry.
17.3: But we command them only: while they are readers, let them marry.
17.4: But then it shall not be possible for them afterwards to be ordained.

18.1: [Topic:] Concerning the priests who strike everyone.
18.2: A bishop or an elder who strikes a Christian or one who does not believe, when he has sinned, and seeks by this deed to make men fear — we command that he be deposed. For the Lord did not command us to do this.
18.3: And not in any place — for when they struck him, he did not strike.
18.4: And when they reviled him, he did not revile.
18.5: And when they afflicted him, he did not take vengeance or become angry.

19.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who is rightly deposed from the clergy.
19.2: If a bishop, or an elder, or a deacon, who has rightly been deposed on account of a manifest sin, becomes obstinate and returns to take possession of his former office [in time of permission?] — let this one depart entirely from the Christian church.

20.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who is ordained through bribery.
20.2: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon takes the grade of the priesthood through bribery, let him be deposed.
20.3: And let the one who ordained him be deposed, and be removed forever from the priestly office; and let them not associate with him in any respect — just as I removed Simon the Magician from me, I, Peter.

21.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who calls in aid that he may take the church.
21.2: If a bishop obtains a position through the princes of this world, and rules the church through them — let him be deposed and expelled: he, and all of them who follow him.

22.1: [Topic:] Concerning the elder who despises the bishop.
22.2: If an elder despises a bishop, and separates himself from him, and builds for himself an altar — although no guilt is found against the bishop in judgment, and in the matter of the service of God he is right — let him be deposed; for he is ambitious for office, he; and also all the priests who follow him, for he is a rebel.
22.3: And the laymen who follow him, let them be expelled.
22.4: And this shall be when the bishop has asked them once, and a second time, and a third time.

23.1: [Topic:] Concerning the elder or the deacon whom the bishop has expelled.
23.2: If a bishop has expelled an elder or a deacon, another bishop shall not allow him to enter again, unless he who expelled him permits it, or if he has died.

24.1: Let a foreign bishop not receive [them] — his elders and his deacons — but let him cut them off; as the inferior clergy — except if they have his permission: let them be ordained and joined.
24.2: And if they are preachers of righteousness, let them enter; but if not, let them give them what they need, and let them not join with them; for many are such — impure.

25.1: [Topic:] It is fitting that the chief of the metropolitans know the bishops of the whole province.
25.2: And it is their duty to know who is the first among them, and they shall call him the metropolitan. And they shall not undertake an important work without the consent of the great one; and they shall do which is their duty according to their dioceses and according to the people who are in their dioceses.
25.3: But he who has been ordained as metropolitan over them, let him not do anything at all without the consent of all the bishops; and thus let them all be one association, and praise God through Christ Jesus and the Holy Spirit.
25.4: And a bishop shall not dare to ordain anyone outside of his diocese, in localities that do not belong to him.
25.5: And if he is found to have done this without the consent of the head — of this place and these villages and cities — let him be deposed, he and those whom he ordained.

26.1: And if he has been ordained as bishop, and does not instruct nor consider the people who were given to him, let him be separated until he learns to instruct.
26.2: And likewise an elder and a deacon.
26.3: But if he has advanced and is not received that he come — and this is not on his account, but on account of the people — let him remain, he, as bishop; but the priests also in the city, let them be separated; for they did not admonish the people as was fitting.

27.1: And let there be a meeting of the bishops twice in a year; and let them examine concerning the ordinance of the divine office, and let them explain concerning the heresies and the offenses which are in the church.
27.2: And the first meeting shall be in the middle of Pentecost; and the second meeting on the 12th of Tekemt.

28.1: And let the bishop take thought concerning the property of the church, and let him manage it as one upon whom God looks.
28.2: And it shall not be his privilege to take profit from them for himself alone.
28.3: And let him not give the property of God to the children of his kindred, even if they are poor.
28.4: And it shall not be his privilege to sell the property of his church on these pretexts.

29.1: [Topic:] Concerning the consultation of the bishop.
29.2: Let none of the elders nor of the deacons do anything, without the advice of the bishop; for he is the one to whom the people of the Lord have been entrusted, and he again it is who will answer concerning their souls.

30.1: And let the property of the bishop be known separately, and the property of the church — lest they fall into famine and curse over his death.

31.1: [Topic:] Concerning the setting of the bishop over the property of the church.
31.2: We command therefore that the bishop be the one who shall have control of the property of the church; for he is the one to whom are entrusted the precious souls of men. What, therefore, is all the property that is given to him, that he should have command over it by his will and should feed the poor with it — through them, by the hand of the elders and the deacons — in the fear of God and in trembling?
31.3: And he shall take for himself of it according to his desire, if he is in need concerning what they ask — from him, the brothers from afar who visit him ask of him — so that he may not lack what they ask of him; for it is a law of God [commanding?] those who serve at the altar, that they shall also be sustained from the altar; for the soldiers of a king will not fight against his enemies at their own sustenance.

32.1: [Topic:] Concerning those who frequent the theatre.
32.2: A bishop or an elder or a deacon who frequents the theatre, or wanders around, or becomes intoxicated — let him cease; but if not, let him be expelled.
32.3: Sub-deacons, readers, and psalmsingers — if they do this deed, let them cease; but if not, let them be expelled.
32.4: And thus also the laymen. A bishop or an elder or a deacon who knows of one that frequents and does not cease, is in duty bound to prevent him; but if not, let him be deposed.

33.1: A bishop or an elder or a deacon who attends the baptism of the heretics or their eucharist — we command that he be deposed.
33.2: For what communion has Christ with Satan? Or what part have believers with those who do not believe?

34.1: [Topic:] Concerning the condition of him who regards marriage as impure.
34.2: But if a bishop or an elder or a deacon, or one of the ordained priests, refuses marriage, or to eat food, or to drink wine — and it is not on account of temperance, but because these are impure, although the Scriptures establish all these things as good, and God created man male and female — and such an one thus blasphemes: let him cease; but if not, let him be deposed, and let him depart from the church.

35.1: [Topic:] Concerning the deposing of him who does not receive those who repent of their sins.
35.2: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon is not willing to receive him who has repented of his sins, let him be deposed; for he grieves the heart of our Lord, who says: there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner that repents.

36.1: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon will not eat a little food and drink a small measure of wine during the festival days, and in secret considers these things wrong, and becomes a cause of offense to the people — let him be deposed.

37.1: If one of the priests has been found eating or drinking in a place of public resort, let him be separated; except if it is in an inn for strangers on account of the needs of travel.
37.2: And if one of the ordained curses a bishop, let him be deposed; for it is said: You shall not curse the leader of your people.
37.3: And if one of the lower clergy curses an elder or a deacon, let him be expelled.
37.4: And if one of the priests ridicules a deaf person, or a lame one, or a blind one, or one deformed in his foot, let him be expelled.
37.5: And thus also a layman, if he does this.

38.1: [Topic:] Concerning the bishop or elder who does not teach the people to serve the Lord.
38.2: A bishop or an elder who neglects the clergy and the laity, and does not teach them the service of the Lord — let him be removed; and if he continues in his neglect, let him be deposed.

39.1: If a bishop or an elder is neglectful in reference to him who is poor from among the clergy, and does not make him his equal by giving to him according to his desire — let him be removed.
39.2: And if he continues in his neglect, let him be deposed like him who slays his brother.

40.1: If there is one who spreads the writings which the heretics have written in falsehood, and brings them into the church as holy writings, in order to entrap the people and the clergy — let him be deposed.

41.1: [Topic:] Concerning the priest whom the people convict of sexual immorality or something else.
41.2: If there is a dispute among the believers with regard to sexual immorality, or luxurious life, or other fault, and they convict him — he shall no longer be among the clergy.

42.1: [Topic:] Concerning the denial of Christ and the denial of the priesthood.
42.2: If any of the clergy denies on account of the fear of man — either of the Jews, or of the gentiles, or of the heretics — and if it is the name of Christ which he has denied, let him be removed; and if it is the name of the priesthood, let him be deposed.
42.3: And if he repents, they shall receive him, and he shall enter as a layman.

43.1: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon, or one of the ordained clergy, eats food in which there is the blood of its life, or which has not been slaughtered, or of which a beast has bitten, or which has been found dead — let him be deposed, as the law commands in regard to this.
43.2: And if he is a layman, let him be expelled.

44.1: If any of the clergy has been discovered fasting on the Lord's day or on the Sabbath day — except on the great Sabbath alone which is the Passah — let him be deposed.

45.1: If one of the clergy or a layman enters the synagogue of the Jews or the place of the heretics in order to pray — let the priests be deposed, and the layman, let him be expelled.

46.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who strikes a man until he dies, and him who overpowers a virgin.
46.2: If a priest has a quarrel with another and strikes him, and he dies — let him be deposed on account of the hardness of his heart; and in the case of a layman, let him be expelled.
46.3: And if a layman has violated a virgin before she has been promised, and has cohabited with her — let him be expelled.
46.4: And he shall not marry another, but he shall abide with her whom he has forced, even if she is poor and deformed.

47.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who is ordained a second time.
47.2: If [it is found that?] a bishop or an elder or a deacon has been ordained a second time, let him be deposed, he too — as also the one who ordained him; unless indeed it is certain that they were ordained by heretics: for it will never be that they who have been baptized or ordained by such men will become believers or clergy.

48.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who does not fast in the forty [days], and on the fourth [day?], and on the sixth [day?].
48.2: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon, or a reader or a psalm-singer, does not fast in the holy forty days and on the fourth and the sixth, let him be deposed — except if illness of body prevents him.
48.3: And in the case of a layman, let him be expelled.

49.1: If a bishop or an elder or a deacon, or any of the clergy, fasts with the Jews, or celebrates the Passah with them, or accepts from them of their festival [gifts?] — leaven or whatever is like it — let him be deposed; and in the case of a layman, let him be expelled.
49.2: And if a layman brings oil or lamps into the temple of the gentiles or the synagogue of the Jews, let him be expelled.

50.1: [Topic:] Concerning him who steals the oil or the wax or anything that is the property of the church.
50.2: If any of the clergy steals the wax belonging to the church, or the oil, let him be deposed; and what he has stolen he shall refund fivefold.
50.3: Silver vessels and clothes — if they have been seen a few days — no man shall take from them anything for himself alone; for this action is a sin.
50.4: And he who does this shall be expelled, and they shall punish him.

51.1: [Topic:] Concerning the bishop whom they have accused.
51.2: When men — believing, truthful and good — have accused a bishop, it is necessary that he be called before the bishops.
51.3: And if he comes and confesses his sins, they shall again take him and pass over him a judgment which is just.
51.4: And if they call him and he does not come, they shall call him a second time, and two bishops shall go as messengers to him.
51.5: And if he does not obey, they shall call him a third time and shall again send two bishops to him as messengers.
51.6: And if he does not obey, and is rebellious and does not come — those who have assembled shall pass judgment over him according to what is right, that he shall be as one whom they have convicted, because he has fled from judgment.

52.1: That they shall not listen to the testimony of a heretic against a bishop, and shall not listen to a single person.
52.2: The testimony of a heretic shall not be received against a bishop, and the testimony of a single person shall not be received; for by the mouth of two and three shall every matter stand.
52.3: Nor shall it be lawful for a bishop to bestow the office of bishop upon his brother or his son or his kindred.
52.4: Nor shall he ordain whomsoever he pleases; for it is not right that the episcopal dignity shall be inherited: nor shall he give away the property of the Lord for the sake of the will of men, for it is not allowed to make the church of Christ an inheritance.
52.5: For if they do thus, and thus take to themselves of the office, they will be as though they were naught; and they shall be judged with justice.
52.6: If he is one-eyed or lame in his foot, and he is worthy — let him be ordained [as bishop?]; for a defect of the body does not corrupt him, but a defect of the soul [does].
52.7: A deaf and a blind man, however, shall not be ordained as a bishop — not as being unclean, but lest the property of the church be scattered.
52.8: He who is possessed of a demon shall not be ordained [as] priest, and shall not pray with the believers.
52.9: And if he is purified, they shall admit him; and if he is worthy, let him be ordained [as] priest.

53.1: Let not a bishop be ordained who has been newly baptized.
53.2: He who has come from among the gentiles, or has been living in sins and has been baptized, shall not be ordained as bishop at once; nor is it allowed that he who has not been tried shall become the teacher of other men — but he shall become this by the grace of God.
53.3: Nor shall it be allowed the bishop that he shall gather and accumulate wealth; but he shall be found [as] a servant of the church; but if not, he shall not perform the episcopal office.
53.4: There is no one who can serve two masters, according to the command of our Lord.
53.5: And we command that no servant shall be ordained [as] priest but with the consent of his master, lest his master be offended; for in this way the households are diminished.
53.6: And if ever there is found a servant in his time who is worthy of the station of ordination — as there has appeared to us Onesimus — and his master sets him free and lets him go forth from his household, let him be ordained.

54.1: A bishop or an elder or a deacon who connects himself with the army, and desires to perform these two offices — that he should take a human office and take the priestly office — let him be deposed. For it is said: Give to God that which is God's, and to the king that which is the king's.
54.2: He who despises the king or the magistrate, except with justice — him they shall punish.
54.3: If it is one of the clergy, he shall be deposed; and if a layman, he shall be expelled.

55.1: [Topic:] Concerning which books of the Old and of the New [Testaments] are to be received in the church.
55.2: And these books shall all be sacred and honored to the clergy and to the laity.
55.3: And these indeed are of the Old Testament.

56.1: The writings of Moses: Genesis; Exodus; Leviticus; Numbers; Deuteronomy. Joshua the son of Nun. Judges. Ruth. 8 books of Kings — the first and the second; 6 books: the third and the fourth. The book of the chronicles of the kings. Ezra, first and second. The book of Job. Esther. Tobit. Ecclesiastes. 150 psalms. Of the church, of the council (gloss?). The Song of Songs. The twelve minor prophets. Isaiah. Jeremiah. Daniel. Ezekiel.
56.3: Besides these: the wisdom of Solomon. Judith. And the books of Kufale [Jubilees]. Jesus the son of Sirach, the very wise.
56.4: And these are the books of the new law: 4 gospels — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; and the Acts of the Apostles; and 2 letters of Peter; 3 letters of John; the letter of James; the letter of Jude; 14 letters of Paul; and the Apocalypse which is the vision of John; and 2 letters of Clement.

57.1: [Topic:] Concerning the Canons of the Apostles.
57.2: This we command you, O bishops, in reference to the Synodus: for if you listen to it, you shall be saved and delivered, and there shall be peace to you forever.
57.3: But if you do not obey this and do not receive what is in this, [the Lord] will scorn you, and there shall be sadness in your midst forever.
57.4: And afterwards you shall meet with the judgment which you deserve on account of your transgression.
57.5: And may God, the only one, and his only Son Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit, the Maker of all creation, give to each one of you peace, and may he help you with all good things; and may you not faint, but be without stain, having no sin.
57.6: And may he make you worthy of a place in eternal life, through his Son whom he loves, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Living one, the Savior — to whom is glory with the Father and with the Holy Spirit to all eternity. Amen.
57.7: This is the Synodus of the apostles which they sent with Clement; and glory to God forever and ever. Amen.
